title: A ballpoint that would not leak
text: The ballpoint pen was {{1}} by a Hungarian journalist who was tired of blotting paper. Laszlo Biro noticed that newspaper ink {{2}} almost instantly, and reasoned that a pen using it would need a rolling ball rather than a nib. He was right: the ball spreads the thick ink as it turns, and the sealed point {{3}} the leaks that made fountain pens a liability at altitude — a flaw serious enough that the RAF {{4}} thirty thousand pens for its aircrews. The road to the desk drawer was longer than the invention. Biro sold the patent cheaply, a British accountant {{5}} the idea for a decade, and early American versions {{6}} so badly that the invention became a byword for disappointment before a French businessman named Marcel Bich bought the rights, {{7}} production costs to pennies, and gave the world the Bic. Today some two million biros are sold every day. Few objects {{8}} the principle better: a sphere in a socket, ink that dries on contact, and a design that has barely changed in eighty years because it cannot be improved.

gaps.explanation: 'was invented by a Hungarian journalist' — created by him; intervene = come between, invert = turn upside down.
'newspaper ink dried almost instantly' — lost its wetness, the property Biro exploited; drone = speak in a dull monotone.
'the sealed point eliminated the leaks' — removed them entirely; elongate = lengthen.
'the RAF ordered thirty thousand pens' — placed an order for them; ordain = decree or make someone a priest.
'an accountant shelved the idea for a decade' — put it on a shelf, figuratively; shirk = avoid work.
'early versions leaked so badly' — let ink escape, the very flaw the ballpoint had solved; loaf = idle about.
'cutting production costs to pennies' — slashing them; court = seek the favour of.
'few objects embody the principle better' — give it a physical form; embark takes 'on'.
